title: POST /auth (CreateToken)
text:
Creates a new auth token to use for access to the PUT and DELETE /booking

Parameters:
- username (String) [Request body]: Username for authentication
- password (String) [Request body]: Password for authentication

Headers:
- Content-Type (string) [Header]: Sets the format of payload you are sending

Request examples:
Example 1:
curl -X POST \
  https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/auth \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "username" : "admin",
    "password" : "password123"
}'

Success response:
- token (String) [Success 200]: Token to use in future requests
Response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK

{
    "token": "abc123"
}

title: POST /booking (CreateBooking)
text:
Creates a new booking in the API

Parameters:
- firstname (String) [Request body]: Firstname for the guest who made the booking
- lastname (String) [Request body]: Lastname for the guest who made the booking
- totalprice (Number) [Request body]: The total price for the booking
- depositpaid (Boolean) [Request body]: Whether the deposit has been paid or not
- bookingdates.checkin (Date) [Request body]: Date the guest is checking in
- bookingdates.checkout (Date) [Request body]: Date the guest is checking out
- additionalneeds (String) [Request body]: Any other needs the guest has

Headers:
- Content-Type (string) [Header]: Sets the format of payload you are sending. Can be application/json or text/xml
- Accept (string) [Header]: Sets what format the response body is returned in. Can be application/json or application/xml

Request examples:
JSON example usage:
curl -X POST \
  https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "firstname" : "Jim",
    "lastname" : "Brown",
    "totalprice" : 111,
    "depositpaid" : true,
    "bookingdates" : {
        "checkin" : "2018-01-01",
        "checkout" : "2019-01-01"
    },
    "additionalneeds" : "Breakfast"
}'

XML example usage:
curl -X POST \
  https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking \
  -H 'Content-Type: text/xml' \
  -d '<booking>
    <firstname>Jim</firstname>
    <lastname>Brown</lastname>
    <totalprice>111</totalprice>
    <depositpaid>true</depositpaid>
    <bookingdates>
      <checkin>2018-01-01</checkin>
      <checkout>2019-01-01</checkout>
    </bookingdates>
    <additionalneeds>Breakfast</additionalneeds>
  </booking>'

URLencoded example usage:
curl -X POST \
  https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'firstname=Jim&lastname=Brown&totalprice=111&depositpaid=true&bookingdates%5Bcheckin%5D=2018-01-01&bookingdates%5Bcheckout%5D=2018-01-02'

Success response:
- bookingid (Number) [Success 200]: ID for newly created booking
- booking (Object) [Success 200]: Object that contains
- booking.firstname (String) [Success 200]: Firstname for the guest who made the booking
- booking.lastname (String) [Success 200]: Lastname for the guest who made the booking
- booking.totalprice (Number) [Success 200]: The total price for the booking
- booking.depositpaid (Boolean) [Success 200]: Whether the deposit has been paid or not
- booking.bookingdates (Object) [Success 200]: Sub-object that contains the checkin and checkout dates
- booking.bookingdates.checkin (Date) [Success 200]: Date the guest is checking in
- booking.bookingdates.checkout (Date) [Success 200]: Date the guest is checking out
- booking.additionalneeds (String) [Success 200]: Any other needs the guest has

title: DELETE /booking/1 (DeleteBooking)
text:
Deletes a booking from the API. Requires an authorization token to be set in the header or a Basic auth header.

Parameters:
- id (Number) [Url Parameter]: ID for the booking you want to update

Headers:
- Cookie (string, optional) [Header]: Sets an authorization token to access the DELETE endpoint, can be used as an alternative to the Authorization
- Authorization (string, optional) [Header]: YWRtaW46cGFzc3dvcmQxMjM=]   Basic authorization header to access the DELETE endpoint, can be used as an alternative to the Cookie header

Request examples:
Example 1 (Cookie):
curl -X DELETE \
  https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Cookie: token=abc123'

Example 2 (Basic auth):
curl -X DELETE \
  https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking/1 \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Basic YWRtaW46cGFzc3dvcmQxMjM='

Success response:
- OK (String) [Success 200]: Default HTTP 201 response
Response:
HTTP/1.1 201 Created

title: GET /booking (GetBookingIds)
text:
Returns the ids of all the bookings that exist within the API. Can take optional query strings to search and return a subset of booking ids.

Parameters:
- firstname (String, optional) [Parameter]: Return bookings with a specific firstname
- lastname (String, optional) [Parameter]: Return bookings with a specific lastname
- checkin (date, optional) [Parameter]: Return bookings that have a checkin date greater than or equal to the set checkin date. Format must be CCYY-MM-DD
- checkout (date, optional) [Parameter]: Return bookings that have a checkout date greater than or equal to the set checkout date. Format must be CCYY-MM-DD

Request examples:
Example 1 (All IDs):
curl -i https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking

Example 2 (Filter by name):
curl -i https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking?firstname=sally&lastname=brown

Example 3 (Filter by checkin/checkout date):
curl -i https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/booking?checkin=2014-03-13&checkout=2014-05-21

Success response:
- object (object[]) [Success 200]: Array of objects that contain unique booking IDs
- object.bookingid (number) [Success 200]: ID of a specific booking that matches search criteria
Response:
HTTP/1.1 200 OK

[
  {
    "bookingid": 1
  },
  {
    "bookingid": 2
  },
  {
    "bookingid": 3
  },
  {
    "bookingid": 4
  }
]

title: GET /ping (HealthCheck)
text:
A simple health check endpoint to confirm whether the API is up and running.

Request examples:
Ping server:
curl -i https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/ping

Success response:
- OK (String) [Success 200]: Default HTTP 201 response
Response:
HTTP/1.1 201 Created

title: Naming requests
text:
Number every request with two digits so the run order is obvious: "01 Login", "02 Create booking".
Mark requests that expect a rejection or an empty result with "(negative)" at the end of the name.

title: Test data
text:
Never rely on bookings that already exist on the server; the demo data is reset regularly and other people change it.
Create the data each collection needs, with names made unique by a timestamp or random suffix.
Use check-in and check-out dates in the future.

title: Cleanup
text:
Every booking a collection creates must be deleted by that collection.
After deleting, add a request that reads the booking again and expects 404, to prove the cleanup worked.

title: Order of assertions
text:
In each test script, assert the status code first, then the shape of the body, then specific values.
Give every pm.test a name that says what is expected, for example "Status is 200" or "Only additionalneeds changed".

title: Variables
text:
Keep the base URL in a collection variable named baseUrl.
Pass values between requests with pm.collectionVariables, never by hard-coding ids or tokens.

title: Known quirks of Restful-Booker
text:
A successful DELETE answers 201, not 200 or 204.
Login with wrong credentials answers 200 with {"reason":"Bad credentials"} instead of 401.
Update and delete without credentials answer 403.
These are the API's real behaviour, so tests assert them as they are.

title: Known API bugs
text:
When the knowledge base lists a known API bug, still assert the behaviour the API documentation describes.
The test is meant to fail until the API is fixed; never write a test that expects the buggy behaviour.

id: known-issues.md:Known API bug: GET /booking?checkin=YYYY-MM-DD leaves out bookings whose checkin equals the given date (it acts as strictly after), although the docs say on or after.
title: Known API bug: GET /booking?checkin=YYYY-MM-DD leaves out bookings whose checkin equals the given date (it acts as strictly after), although the docs say on or after.
text:
Docs: checkin filter returns bookings with checkin "greater than or equal to" the date. Created booking 2081 with checkin 2027-01-01. GET /booking?checkin=2027-01-01 returned [{"bookingid":1599}] (2081 missing). GET /booking?checkin=2026-12-31 returned [1599, 2081]. So the filter is strictly greater-than and leaves out same-day check-ins, which contradicts the docs.
Found 2026-11-19 in "05b Filter by checkin date (same day)".

id: known-issues.md:Test pitfall: PUT /booking/:id returns 403 Forbidden unless a Cookie token=... or Basic Authorization header is sent, so every update request needs the auth header.
title: Test pitfall: PUT /booking/:id returns 403 Forbidden unless a Cookie token=... or Basic Authorization header is sent, so every update request needs the auth header.
text:
The request 07 definition sends only the Content-Type and Accept headers, with no Cookie and no Authorization. Requests 08 and 09 send "Cookie: token={{token}}". Probe: PUT /booking/2081 without a Cookie returned 403 "Forbidden". The same PUT with "Cookie: token=bd3b3839fb149c5" returned 200 with totalprice 200. Docs: PUT needs either a Cookie token or Basic Authorization.
Fix: Add the header "Cookie: token={{token}}" to 07, as 08 and 09 already do.
Found 2026-11-19 in "07 Update booking (full)".

id: known-issues.md:Test pitfall: DELETE /booking/:id returns 201 Created on success, as documented, not 200.
title: Test pitfall: DELETE /booking/:id returns 201 Created on success, as documented, not 200.
text:
The docs for DELETE /booking/:id show the response "HTTP/1.1 201 Created". Probe: DELETE /booking/2081 with the Cookie token returned 201 "Created". In the run, the follow-up GET (request 10) returned 404, so the delete works. The test expects 200, which the docs do not support.
Fix: Expect status 201 (Created) for a successful DELETE.
Found 2026-11-19 in "09 Delete booking".

id: known-issues.md:Test pitfall: Request 08 (PATCH /booking/:id) asserts totalprice 200, which depends on request 07 (PUT) succeeding first. If 07 fails, 08 fails as a consequence, so fix 07 rather than 08.
title: Test pitfall: Request 08 (PATCH /booking/:id) asserts totalprice 200, which depends on request 07 (PUT) succeeding first. If 07 fails, 08 fails as a consequence, so fix 07 rather than 08.
text:
Request 08 is correct. It failed because 07 never updated the price (07 got 403 for the missing token), so totalprice was still 150. Probe: after an authenticated PUT set totalprice to 200, PATCH /booking/1645 {"additionalneeds":"Late checkout"} with the Cookie token returned 200 with totalprice 200, firstname Asha and additionalneeds "Late checkout". So the PATCH works as documented.
Fix: Do not change 08. Adding the Cookie token header to 07 fixes this.
Found 2026-11-19 in "08 Update booking (partial)".

id: known-issues.md:Known API bug: GET /user/login returns its session message as raw text labelled Content-Type application/json, which is not valid JSON, although the contract says application/json with schema string.
title: Known API bug: GET /user/login returns its session message as raw text labelled Content-Type application/json, which is not valid JSON, although the contract says application/json with schema string.
text:
Direct probe with real seeded credentials and no unresolved variables: GET /user/login?username=user1&password=XXXXXXXXXXX with Accept: application/json returns 200, Content-Type application/json, body `Logged in user session: 5415229380296914791`. That is raw text, not valid JSON, so JSON parsing fails ("Unexpected token 'L'"). Contract violation: 200 content application/json has schema {type: string}, so the body should be a JSON string literal, e.g. "\"Logged in user session: ...\"". The unresolved {{username}}/{{password}} in the collection is a separate test defect (the username and password environment variables should be set), but it does not cause this failure: the body is identical with valid credentials.
Found 2026-11-23 in "TC11 Log in with a valid username and password" (Petstore Test).

id: known-issues.md:Known API bug: GET /user/login never checks credentials: a wrong password or a user that does not exist still gets 200 and a session token, although the contract documents 400 for invalid username/password.
title: Known API bug: GET /user/login never checks credentials: a wrong password or a user that does not exist still gets 200 and a session token, although the contract documents 400 for invalid username/password.
text:
Direct probe with an existing seeded user: GET /user/login?username=user1&password=wrong-password-xyz returns 200 "Logged in user session: 7831645696840774914". Contract violation: GET /user/login responses say '400: Invalid username/password supplied'. The unresolved {{username}} is a separate test defect: set the username environment variable so the test really sends an existing user. Fixing it would not change the result, because a real user with a wrong password also gets 200.
Found 2026-11-23 in "TC12 Log in with a wrong password" (Petstore Test).

id: known-issues.md:Known API bug: GET /user/login on petstore3.swagger.io returns 200 and a session for any username and password, even ones that do not exist or are missing, and never the documented 400 "Invalid username/password supplied".
title: Known API bug: GET /user/login on petstore3.swagger.io returns 200 and a session for any username and password, even ones that do not exist or are missing, and never the documented 400 "Invalid username/password supplied".
text:
Direct probe: GET /user/login?username=nonexistent_user_zz9&password=whatever returned 200 with the body "Logged in user session: 3956666403132616035". GET /user/login with no parameters also returned 200 with a session. Contract violation: GET /user/login documents 400 "Invalid username/password supplied", but the API accepts any credentials, including none. The test's URL, parameters and expected value match the contract.
Found 2026-11-23 in "KNOWN BUG - TC13 Log in with a username that does not exist" (Petstore Test).
